subtitle: Al-Biruni and the Measured Gaze Upon India

panels.shot: dramatic three-quarter view, medium close-up, Al-Biruni seated amid scrolls, one hand on an open notebook, Indian star map behind him
panels.action: Al-Biruni sits in a dim study, turbaned and bearded, pen poised over a notebook, surrounded by Arabic and Sanskrit manuscripts while a painted Indian cosmos arcs across the wall behind him.

dialogue.text: In an age of sword and conquest, one outsider in Ghazni opened a notebook and measured India with questions, not weapons: Abu Rayhan al-Biruni, c. 1017–1030.

i18n.hi: तलवारों और फ़तह के ज़माने में, ग़ज़नी के एक बाहरी ने हथियार नहीं, नोटबुक से भारत को नापा – अबू रैयान अल-बिरूनी, लगभग 1017–1030.

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over Ghazni, wide shot
panels.action: A sweeping view of Ghazni’s palaces and mosques under a clear sky, caravans entering the city; in a balcony alcove, Al-Biruni watches, clutching a small notebook.

dialogue.text: From the city of Ghazni, under Sultan Mahmud, caravans carried plunder and prisoners from raids into northwestern India. Al-Biruni watched, not as a general, but as a scientist of the age.

i18n.hi: ग़ज़नी के शहर से, सुल्तान महमूद के राज में, कारवाँ लूट और क़ैदियों को उत्तर-पश्चिमी भारत से घसीट लाते थे। अल-बिरूनी ये सब देखता था – सेनापति नहीं, उस दौर का वैज्ञानिक बनकर।

panels.shot: slow push-in, medium shot in study
panels.action: Inside a modest chamber stacked with astronomical instruments and books, Al-Biruni sits cross-legged by a low desk, comparing a brass astrolabe with a rough sketch of the horizon.

dialogue.text: Trained in the Arabic–Persian world of astronomy and mathematics, he had already weighed the earth, traced eclipses, and debated Greek and Muslim thinkers. Yet India, close and unknown, troubled him.

i18n.hi: अरबी–फ़ारसी दुनिया की खगोल और गणित में तराशा हुआ, वो धरती का वज़न नाप चुका था, ग्रहणों की चाल लिख चुका था, यूनानी और मुस्लिम विद्वानों से बहस कर चुका था। फिर भी पास का, अनजाना भारत उसे बेचैन करता था।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Al-Biruni’s eyes over a pile of Indian objects
panels.action: Al-Biruni studies an Indian bronze idol and a palm-leaf manuscript newly arrived from the raids, his eyes intent, fingers resting on blank pages of his notebook.

dialogue.text: Temple bronzes, palm-leaf manuscripts, and captive Brahmins arrived in Ghazni as trophies. To al-Biruni they were something else: evidence, fragments of a vast and ordered knowledge.

i18n.hi: मंदिर के काँसे, ताल-पत्र पांडुलिपियाँ और पकड़े गए ब्राह्मण, ग़ज़नी में घमंड के गहने बनकर आए। अल-बिरूनी के लिए ये कुछ और थे – सबूत, एक विशाल, सधे हुए ज्ञान के टुकड़े।

panels.shot: low-angle interior of court library, wide shot
panels.action: In a grand hall lined with shelves, Al-Biruni stands before a group of scholars and officials, holding up a palm-leaf manuscript with distant Indian script, his notebook tucked in his belt.

dialogue.text: He knew Greek treatises translated into Arabic and older Indian works already rendered as Sindhind tables. But these leaves spoke in a language he did not yet know. He chose the hardest path.

i18n.hi: वो यूनानी किताबें जानता था जो अरबी में आई थीं, और पुराने भारतीय ग्रंथ जो ‘सिंधिंद’ सारणियों में ढल चुके थे। लेकिन ये पत्ते किसी और ज़बान में बोलते थे, जो उसे नहीं आती थी। उसने वही मुश्किल रास्ता चुना।

panels.shot: intimate indoor close-up, candlelit, Al-Biruni with Brahmin teacher implied off-frame
panels.action: By lamplight in a quiet room, Al-Biruni leans forward over a palm-leaf, murmuring strange sounds as a hand from off-frame points to Sanskrit letters.

dialogue.text: In India, he sought Brahmin teachers and learned Sanskrit. He admits the struggle in his own book: Indian sciences are locked in a language and guarded by men wary of foreigners.

i18n.hi: भारत आकर उसने ब्राह्मण गुरुओं को ढूँढ़ा और संस्कृत सीखी। अपनी किताब में खुद मानता है: भारतीय विद्या एक भाषा में बंद है, ऐसे लोगों की रखवाली में जो परदेसी से सतर्क हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot, Al-Biruni writing, palm-leaf and Arabic codex side by side
panels.action: Al-Biruni sits at a desk with a Sanskrit astronomical text open, an Arabic notebook beside it; he carefully copies a diagram of planetary orbits, noting Indian numerals and terms.

dialogue.text: Slowly, he compared Sanskrit verses on planets and eclipses with Ptolemaic models in Arabic. Where India used sine tables, where Greek geometry triumphed, he recorded both without flattery.

i18n.hi: धीरे-धीरे उसने ग्रहों और ग्रहणों पर संस्कृत श्लोकों की तुलना अरबी में प्टोलेमी की योजनाओं से की। जहाँ भारत ने ज्या-सारणीें बनाईं, जहाँ यूनानी ज्यामिति भारी पड़ी – दोनों को वो बिना चापलूसी दर्ज करता गया।

panels.shot: wide shot of Indian scholarly gathering under a tree
panels.action: Under a large tree near an Indian temple-complex, Al-Biruni sits on the ground among robed Indian scholars; they gesture towards the sky as he listens, notebook open on his lap.

dialogue.text: “If you would judge us,” an elder says, “learn to recite as we do.”

i18n.hi: “अगर हमें आँकना है,” एक बुज़ुर्ग कहता है, “तो पहले हमारी तरह बोलना सीखो।”

panels.shot: medium shot, respectful distance, Al-Biruni outside a temple gate
panels.action: Al-Biruni waits at the threshold of an Indian temple courtyard; Brahmin scholars stand inside, some curious, some withdrawn; he bows slightly, keeping his notebook close but closed.

dialogue.text: He notes the barriers plainly: caste rules, suspicion of Muslims, reluctance to share sacred lore. Still, some scholars debated him, and from those debates he wrested careful descriptions.

i18n.hi: वो रुकावटें साफ़ लिखता है: जाति की दीवारें, मुसलमानों पर शक, पवित्र ज्ञान बाँटने से झिझक। फिर भी कुछ पंडित उससे बहस पर उतरे, और उन बहसों से उसने बड़ी सावधानी से विवरण खींच लिए।

panels.action: From behind Al-Biruni, the viewer sees his notebook filled with neat Arabic script summarizing Indian mathematics, with margins marked ‘excellent’, ‘obscure’, ‘contradictory’.

dialogue.text: In Kitab al-Hind, written around 1030, he insists: he will present Indian ideas as they see themselves, like a translator, then weigh them. Praise and critique share the same page.

i18n.hi: किताब अल-हिन्द में, जो 1030 के आसपास लिखी, वो ज़िद करता है: भारतीय विचारों को पहले वैसे ही पेश करूँगा, जैसे वे खुद को देखते हैं – एक अनुवादक की तरह; फिर तौलूँगा। तारीफ़ और सवाल एक ही पन्ने पर चलते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot, Al-Biruni at ground with geometric diagram
panels.action: On packed earth, Al-Biruni draws a circle and triangle with a stick, next to an Indian scholar’s diagram; both men compare angles, with the ruins of a pillaged city hazy in the background.

dialogue.text: He marvels at Indian arithmetic, algebra, and the use of zero, at their long chronology and subtle metaphysics. Yet he points out contradictions in cosmology and exaggerations in their ages of the world.

i18n.hi: वो भारतीय गणित, बीजगणित और शून्य के इस्तेमाल पर हैरान होता है, उनकी लंबी काल-गणना और बारीक दर्शन पर भी। पर साथ ही ब्रह्मांड-विद्या की उलझनों और युगों की बढ़ाई हुई उम्रों पर उँगली रख देता है।

panels.shot: low-angle shot, Al-Biruni observing a solar eclipse with instruments
panels.action: On a hilltop, Al-Biruni, flanked by simple Indian and Arabic instruments, watches a partial eclipse, making notes as temple bells sound faintly from the valley.

dialogue.text: His own measurements of eclipses and meridian arcs gave him confidence. India’s observations he respected; sometimes their numbers matched his, sometimes they erred. He recorded both with a steady hand.

i18n.hi: ग्रहणों और मध्यान्ह रेखा के अपने माप उसे यक़ीन देते थे। भारत की देखी-नापी चीज़ों को उसने सम्मान दिया – कई बार उनके अंक उसके जैसे निकले, कई बार चूके। दोनों ही को उसने एक स्थिर कलम से दर्ज किया।

panels.shot: interior study wide shot, walls covered in maps and tables
panels.action: Al-Biruni sits amid a forest of hanging tables of sines, planetary positions, and calendars, some labeled in Arabic, some in Sanskrit script; he arranges them in an orderly sequence in his notebook.

dialogue.text: Around him spread a network of knowledge: Arabic revisions of Greek astronomy, earlier Indian tables like Sindhind, his own critiques. Kitab al-Hind did not start this exchange, but it sharpened its mirror.

i18n.hi: उसके चारों तरफ़ फैला था ज्ञान का जाल: यूनानी खगोल के अरबी रूप, पहले के भारतीय ‘सिंधिंद’ सारणीें, और खुद उसकी टीकाएँ। किताब अल-हिन्द ने ये अदला-बदली शुरू नहीं की, पर इस आईने को तेज़ ज़रूर कर दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot, Al-Biruni writing with intense focus
panels.action: Close on Al-Biruni’s hand as he writes the title of his book, with sections listed: religion, sciences, society, chronology; his face above is weary yet intent.

dialogue.text: He divides his work: Indian religion and philosophy, astronomy and mathematics, customs and calendars. He admits his own Islamic lens, but also rebukes his peers for lazy prejudice.

i18n.hi: वो अपनी किताब बाँटता है: धर्म और दर्शन, खगोल और गणित, रीति और कैलेंडर। वो अपनी इस्लामी नज़र मानता है, लेकिन अपने साथियों की आलसी तंग-नज़री पर चोट भी करता है।

panels.shot: slow push-out from shelf of manuscripts, time-lapse feel
panels.action: A shelf holds a copy of Kitab al-Hind among other Arabic works; dust motes drift in a shaft of light, hinting at centuries passing as the book rests, then is reopened by unseen later hands.

dialogue.text: For centuries, scholars in the Islamic world read his India, long before Europeans rediscovered it in translation. He did not ‘bring India to Europe’, but he kept a demanding record alive.

i18n.hi: सदियों तक इस्लामी दुनिया के विद्वान उसकी ‘भारत’ पढ़ते रहे, बहुत पहले, जब यूरोप ने इसे फिर से अनुवाद में पाया। उसने ‘भारत को यूरोप तक नहीं पहुँचाया’, लेकिन एक सख़्त रिकॉर्ड जिंदा रखा।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on marginal note in his hand
panels.action: Zoomed in on a margin where Al-Biruni has written a terse line comparing an Indian proof with a Greek one, his script steady, a faint smudge from his fingertip beside it.

dialogue.text: “Truth is not owned; it is sought.”

i18n.hi: “सच किसी की मिल्कियत नहीं, ये तलाश है।”

panels.shot: wide contemplative shot, Al-Biruni alone under night sky
panels.action: On a rooftop in Ghazni, Al-Biruni sits alone, notebook closed beside him, gazing at the stars that shine equally over India and his own city.

dialogue.text: Al-Biruni’s legacy is not a single discovery, but a stance: to cross into another world by learning its language, weighing its reasons, and writing with respect and doubt in the same line.

i18n.hi: अल-बिरूनी की विरासत कोई एक खोज नहीं, बल्कि एक अंदाज़ है: दूसरी दुनिया में उसके ही शब्द सीखकर जाना, उसके तर्क तौलना, और आदर और संशय को एक ही लाइन में लिखना।

title_i18n.en: The Scholar Who Brought a Notebook
title_i18n.hi: वो विद्वान जिसने साथ रखी नोटबुक

subtitle_i18n.en: Al-Biruni and the Measured Gaze Upon India
